title: A bar is 12 units long. Did 12 vehicles pass?
description: A horizontal bar for the busiest hour at a Delhi crossing is twelve units long, and one unit stands for one hundred vehicles. Reading the scale first and then multiplying gives the count, and Keeko's doubt, that the length of the bar is the number of vehicles, is checked against the scale.
teaching_notes: One idea: the scale says what one unit of length stands for, so the count is the number of units times that value. Watch for students who read the length of the bar as the count.

source: Let us look at an example of vehicular traffic at a busy road crossing in Delhi, which was studied by the traffic police on a particular day. The number of vehicles passing through the crossing each hour from 6 a.m. to 12:00 noon is shown in the bar graph. One unit of length stands for 100 vehicles.
video_script.why: The child learns that a bar of twelve units can stand for a count far bigger than twelve, so the scale must be read first.
video_script.substitution: Multiply the bar length in units by what one unit stands for.
video_script.anchor: the horizontal bar graph of vehicles passing a busy crossing in Delhi in each hour from six in the morning to noon
video_script.wrong_answer: twelve vehicles passed, because the bar is twelve units long
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko reads the length of the bar as the count of vehicles. A unit already stands for one hundred vehicles, so the units must be multiplied.
video_script.payoff_line: Twelve units of length stand for one thousand two hundred vehicles

final_answer.spoken: twelve units stand for one thousand two hundred vehicles

maths_rules: horizontal bar graph of vehicles passing a crossing in each hour from 6 a.m. to 12 noon
scale: 1 unit of length stands for 100 vehicles
the 7 to 8 a.m. bar is 12 units long, so it shows 12 x 100 = 1200 vehicles
slip: 12 units is a length, not 12 vehicles
video_script.design: One idea: read the scale first, then multiply the length by it. The bar graph stays on the board all video, drawn with unit marks and no number labels along the bottom.
